scenario: 系统设计聊到全球用户加载图片和 JS 很慢。你想说「把静态资源放 CDN,在离用户近的边缘节点缓存,缩短往返」,上一轮却卡成 “put the file on a near server”。
scenario_en: In a system-design round, global users load images and JS slowly. You want to say "put static assets on a CDN, cached at edge nodes near the user," but last time you stalled at "put the file on a near server."
q: 「把静态资源放 CDN,在离用户近的边缘节点缓存,缩短往返延迟」怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say "serve static assets from a CDN, cached at edge nodes close to the user"?
options: We put the images on a CDN net, so the user downloads them from a close server, more fast.
So so the CDN, the CDN it caches the files near the user, near the user, so it loads...
We put the static assets on a CDN, so they're cached at edge locations close to the user.
A content delivery network geographically distributes cached assets to edge nodes proximate to end users.
tradeoff: CDN/edge 术语 vs “CDN net、near server” 硬译:前者点名就近缓存的机制,后者暴露术语不熟。
why: 地道说法是 CDN + 把静态资源缓存在靠近用户的 edge 节点,点出就近缓存降低往返延迟。
why_en: Say CDN plus "cached at edge locations close to the user" — that names near-user caching, not a vague "close server."
whenOtherWins: 若是每个用户都不同的动态数据,CDN 缓存意义不大,改在应用层就近缓存。

A content delivery network geographically distributes cached assets to edge nodes proximate to end users.

termDefinitions.meaning: 内容分发网络:把静态资源缓存到全球多个边缘节点,让用户就近取。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A CDN is a network of edge servers that cache static assets worldwide so each user fetches them from a nearby node.

termDefinitions.meaning: 边缘节点:CDN 里离用户最近的缓存服务器,也叫 PoP。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An edge location is the CDN cache server closest to the user, also called a point of presence (PoP).

termDefinitions.meaning: 静态资源:图片、CSS、JS 等不常变、可缓存的文件。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Static assets are files like images, CSS, and JS that rarely change and can be cached.

scenario: 系统设计问缓存写路径怎么保证不丢数据。你想讲清 write-through 同步写库、write-back 先写缓存异步刷库的区别,上轮却卡成 “write to cache first, then… later”。
scenario_en: A round asks how the cache write path avoids data loss. You want to contrast write-through (sync to DB) with write-back (cache first, async flush), but last time you stalled at "write to cache first, then... later."
q: 「write-through 同步写缓存和库、write-back 先写缓存再异步刷库」这组区别怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you contrast write-through (cache+DB together) with write-back (cache now, flush to DB later)?
options: Write-through writes cache and DB together; write-back writes the cache and flushes to the DB later — fast, but a crash loses buffered writes.
Write-pass saves to the cache and the database at the same time, and write-behind save to the cache, database after.
So write-through is is write to both, and write-back is is later, later to the DB, faster but you can lose...
Write-through propagates each write synchronously to both the cache and the durable backing store, whereas write-back defers persistence to the database asynchronously.
tradeoff: write-through/write-back 术语 + 崩溃丢写的机制 vs “write-pass” 错词或打转:前者点名同步 vs 异步的取舍,后者暴露不熟。
why: write-through 同步写缓存和库更安全;write-back 先写缓存异步刷库更快,但崩溃会丢没刷回的写。术语别说成 write-pass。
why_en: Say write-through (sync to cache and DB) vs write-back (cache now, async flush) — the tell is write-back can lose buffered writes on a crash.
whenOtherWins: 若写很少、丢一点也无所谓,直接 write-through 最省心;write-back 的异步刷库复杂度不值当。

termDefinitions.meaning: 写穿透:写操作同步写入缓存和数据库,保证一致但写更慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-through writes to both the cache and the database synchronously — consistent but slower writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写回:先只写缓存,稍后异步批量刷回数据库,更快但崩溃可能丢未刷的写。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write-back (write-behind) writes only the cache first and flushes to the DB asynchronously later — faster, but a crash can lose un-flushed writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓冲写:已写进缓存但还没刷回数据库的那批写,崩溃时会丢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Buffered writes are writes sitting in the cache that haven't been flushed to the DB yet — lost if the process crashes.

scenario: 内存满了要淘汰缓存条目,面试官问你用什么策略。你想区分 LRU 按最久未用、LFU 按访问次数最少来淘汰,上轮却把 LRU 说成 “throw the last used one”。
scenario_en: Memory is full and the interviewer asks your eviction policy. You want to separate LRU (least-recently-used) from LFU (least-frequently-used), but last time you said LRU "throws the last used one."
q: 「LRU 淘汰最久没被访问的,LFU 淘汰访问次数最少的」这组区别怎么说清?
q_en: How do you distinguish LRU (evict least-recently-used) from LFU (evict least-frequently-used)?
options: LRU throws out the last-used one, and LFU throws out the less-frequent one, by the count.
LRU evicts whatever hasn't been touched in the longest time; LFU evicts whatever's been hit the fewest times.
So LRU is is by time, by recency, and LFU is by, by how many times, how many times it's...
LRU evicts the entry bearing the oldest access timestamp, whereas LFU evicts the entry exhibiting the lowest cumulative access frequency.
tradeoff: LRU/LFU + recency vs frequency 的机制 vs “last-used” 说反:前者点名按什么淘汰,后者把最近用的当成要踢的。
why: LRU 按 recency(最久未用)淘汰,LFU 按 frequency(访问次数最少)淘汰;把 LRU 说成 “last-used” 正好说反了。
why_en: LRU evicts by recency (least recently used), LFU by frequency (fewest hits) — "last-used" is exactly backwards.
whenOtherWins: 若访问模式突变、旧热点该快速让位,LRU 更灵敏;LFU 会被历史高频卡住,这时别用 LFU。

So LRU is is by time, by recency, and LFU is by, by how many times, how many times it's...
LRU evicts the entry bearing the oldest access timestamp, whereas LFU evicts the entry exhibiting the lowest cumulative access frequency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最近最少使用:内存满时淘汰最久没被访问的条目。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LRU, Least Recently Used, evicts the entry that hasn't been accessed for the longest time when memory is full.

termDefinitions.meaning: 最不经常使用:淘汰访问次数最少的条目,保留高频热点。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LFU, Least Frequently Used, evicts the entry with the fewest accesses, keeping the most-hit hot items.

termDefinitions.meaning: 淘汰:缓存内存满时按策略踢掉条目,区别于到期 expire。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Eviction is dropping entries by policy when the cache is full — distinct from TTL expiry.

scenario: 新功能要上线,预计首屏流量瞬间涌入。你想说「上线前先把热点数据灌进缓存,别让第一批请求全 miss」,上轮卡成 “make the cache ready first”。
scenario_en: A feature is launching and first-screen traffic will spike instantly. You want to say "pre-load hot data into the cache before launch so the first requests don't all miss," but last time you stalled at "make the cache ready first."
q: 「上线前先给缓存预热,把热点 key 灌进去,避免首批请求全 miss」怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say "pre-warm the cache before launch so the first requests don't all miss"?
options: We heat up the cache first, we fill the hot data in the cache before, so the cache is not cold.
So before launch we we put the data in, the popular data in the cache, in the cache first, so...
Prior to launch we preload the cache with anticipated high-frequency entries to mitigate initial cache misses at scale.
We pre-warm the cache before launch — load the hot keys ahead of time so the first requests don't all miss.
tradeoff: pre-warm + 灌热点 key 的机制 vs “heat up / make ready” 硬译:前者点名上线前预热防冷启动,后者术语不熟。
why: 地道动词是 pre-warm / warm the cache:上线前把热点 key 灌进去,首批请求就不会全 miss 打库;“heat up” 是 Chinglish。
why_en: The verb is pre-warm (warm the cache) — load hot keys before launch so the first requests hit, not miss; "heat up" is Chinglish.
whenOtherWins: 若流量是缓慢爬坡而非瞬间峰值,让缓存自然填充即可,不必专门预热。

termDefinitions.meaning: 预热缓存:上线或高峰前主动把热点数据写进缓存,避免冷启动全 miss。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To pre-warm (warm) the cache is to load hot data in before launch or peak, so you don't start cold with all misses.

termDefinitions.meaning: 冷缓存:缓存刚启动还没数据,请求全部 miss 回源的状态。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A cold cache is a freshly started cache with no data yet, so every request misses and hits the source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 热点 key:访问量最高、最该预先缓存的那批键。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hot keys are the highest-traffic keys — the ones most worth caching ahead of time.

scenario: 面试官问缓存最难的是什么。你想说「invalidation——源数据一变就得失效对应 key,保持缓存和源同步」,上轮卡成 “keep them the same, it's hard”。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what's hardest about caching. You want to say "invalidation — when the source changes you must drop the matching key to keep cache and source in sync," but last time you stalled at "keep them the same, it's hard."
q: 「最难的是 invalidation:源一变就失效对应 key,别继续返回旧值」怎么说出口?
q_en: How do you say "the hard part is invalidation — drop the key when the source changes so you stop serving stale"?
options: The hard thing is the cache clean, we clean the old data when the database change, keep it the same.
So the hard part is is keeping them, keeping them the same, the cache and the DB, when it changes...
The hard part is invalidation — when the source changes we drop the key so we stop serving the stale copy.
Cache invalidation constitutes the principal difficulty of maintaining coherence between cached entries and the authoritative source.
tradeoff: invalidation + 写时失效 key 的机制 vs “cache clean” 硬译或打转:前者点名保持缓存与源同步,后者术语不熟。
why: 术语是 invalidation,写时把对应 key 失效(drop the key on write),才不会继续返回 stale 旧值,别用 cache clean 白描。
why_en: The term is invalidation — "drop the key on write" when the source changes, so you don't serve stale; "cache clean" is Chinglish.
whenOtherWins: 若能接受短暂不一致,靠短 TTL 自然过期就够,不必写时主动 invalidate 每个 key。

termDefinitions.meaningEn: Invalidation is actively marking or deleting the matching cache entry when the source changes, so you don't return stale data.

termDefinitions.meaning: 删除 key:把缓存里那条记录删掉,下次读会 miss 回源刷新。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: To drop the key is to delete that cache entry so the next read misses and refetches from the source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 旧值:缓存里和源已不一致的过期数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stale copy is cached data that no longer matches the source.

termDefinitions.meaning: 权威源:数据库等真正的数据来源,缓存以它为准。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The source of truth is the authoritative store (e.g., the DB) the cache must stay consistent with.

scenario: 某个不存在的用户 ID 被反复查询,每次都穿透缓存打库。你想说「把 not-found 也缓存,加个短 TTL,挡住反复穿透」,上轮卡成 “save the empty result also”。
scenario_en: A nonexistent user ID gets queried over and over, and every lookup punches through to the DB. You want to say "cache the not-found result too, with a short TTL," but last time you stalled at "save the empty result also."
q: 「把查不到的结果也缓存(negative caching),加短 TTL,挡住反复穿透」怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say "do negative caching — cache the not-found with a short TTL to stop repeated pass-through"?
options: We do negative caching — cache the 'not found' with a short TTL, so repeat lookups for a missing key don't hit the DB.
We use a no-result cache, we save the empty answer so the not-exist key don't go to database again.
So so when the key is not there, not there, we we also cache that, cache that, so it won't...
Negative caching entails persisting the absence of a record in order to preclude redundant origin lookups for nonexistent keys.
tradeoff: negative caching + 短 TTL 的机制 vs “no-result cache” 硬译:前者点名连 miss 都缓存挡穿透,后者术语不熟。
why: 术语是 negative caching:把查不到这一结果也缓存,配上短 TTL,反复查不存在的 key 就不再穿透打库。
why_en: The term is negative caching — cache the not-found with a short TTL, so repeat lookups for a missing key stop hitting the DB.
whenOtherWins: 若不存在的 key 很少被重复查询,负缓存意义不大还占内存,直接回源即可。
options_en: We do negative caching — cache the 'not found' with a short TTL, so repeat lookups for a missing key don't hit the DB.
We use a no-result cache, we save the empty answer so the not-exist key don't go to database again.
So so when the key is not there, not there, we we also cache that, cache that, so it won't...
Negative caching entails persisting the absence of a record in order to preclude redundant origin lookups for nonexistent keys.

termDefinitions.meaning: 负缓存:把「查不到」这一结果也缓存起来,通常配短 TTL,避免反复查不存在的 key 都穿透到库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Negative caching is caching the 'not found' result too, usually with a short TTL, so repeated lookups for a missing key don't keep hitting the DB.

termDefinitions.meaning: 穿透:请求在缓存 miss 后直接打到数据库;不存在的 key 每次都穿透最费。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pass-through is a request going straight to the DB on a cache miss; a nonexistent key punching through every time is the costly case.

termDefinitions.meaning: 短 TTL:给负缓存设的较短过期时间,防止长期缓存住「不存在」而错过后来真出现的数据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A short TTL is a brief expiry on the negative entry, so you don't cache 'not found' long enough to miss data that appears later.

scenario: 一批 key 在同一时刻批量写入、TTL 相同,到期时会同时失效引发 stampede。你想说「给 TTL 加点 jitter,让它们错开过期」,上轮卡成 “make the TTL a little different”。
scenario_en: A batch of keys is written at the same instant with identical TTLs, so they all expire together and cause a stampede. You want to say "add jitter to the TTL so expirations spread out," but last time you stalled at "make the TTL a little different."
q: 「给 TTL 加 jitter,让批量条目错开过期,别一起失效打库」怎么说地道?
q_en: How do you say "add jitter to the TTL so entries don't all expire at once"?
options: We add a random time to the TTL, so the caches not expire in the same time together, spread it out.
We add jitter to the TTL — some randomness — so keys cached together don't all expire at once and stampede the DB.
So we we make the TTL a little random, a little different, different, so they don't all, all expire...
We introduce stochastic variance into each entry's time-to-live in order to desynchronize otherwise concurrent expirations.
tradeoff: jitter + 错开过期的机制 vs “random time / a little different” 白描:前者点名用抖动防同时失效,后者没术语。
why: 地道说法是 add jitter to the TTL:给过期时间加点随机,批量 key 就错开失效,不会一起到期引发 stampede。
why_en: Say "add jitter to the TTL" — randomize the expiry a bit so a batch of keys stagger their expiry instead of all firing at once.
codeSample:
base_ttl = 300
ttl = base_ttl + random(0, 60)   # add up to 60s of jitter
SET key value EX ttl             # each key lands on a slightly different expiry
whenOtherWins: 若这些 key 本就零散写入、TTL 天然错开,就不必额外加 jitter,收益有限。

termDefinitions.meaning: TTL 抖动:给每个条目的过期时间加一点随机偏移,让原本同时到期的 key 错开失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL jitter adds a small random offset to each entry's expiry so keys that would expire together stagger instead.

termDefinitions.meaning: 缓存踩踏:大量条目同时失效,请求一拥而上回源打库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A stampede (thundering herd) is many entries expiring at once so requests flood the DB together.

termDefinitions.meaning: 存活时间:缓存条目的过期时长,到点自动失效。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: TTL, Time To Live, is how long a cache entry lives before it expires automatically.
